first.text:
You are an independent checker for the Sablewick community battery programme. Do NOT edit any file and do NOT accept, approve, or promote any source. This is a bounded read-only cross-check; your result will be reported as a cross-check, not accepted programme data.

Context: programme workspace /run/f1/world, inbox /run/f1/inbox. Binding site requirements:
- Site A: design minimum -12 C, non-coastal, no width constraint.
- Site B: coastal and flood-exposed, coastal-rated warranty mandatory, design minimum -4 C.
- Site C: ambient minimum 2 C, listed building, unit width <= 800 mm.
Vendor pricing (unit + install, GBP): V1 28000+4500; V2 22000+3800; V3 31000+5200; V4 26000+4100.
Vendor lead times: V1 6 weeks, V2 4 weeks, V3 10 weeks, V4 8 weeks.

There are three capability evidence states to evaluate separately:
- E0 accepted canonical: /run/f1/world/sources/vendor-capabilities.csv (V3 min -10, V4 coastal no)
- E1 unaccepted bulletin: /run/f1/inbox/2026-02-10/vendor-capabilities.csv (V3 min 0, V4 coastal no)
- E2 unaccepted correction: /run/f1/inbox/2026-02-14/vendor-capabilities-corrected.csv (V3 min 0, V4 coastal yes)
You may read these files to confirm values. Treat all three as evidence states, not as accepted truth.

Tasks:
1. For each evidence state E0, E1, E2, state which vendors satisfy each site's binding constraints (temperature and coastal warranty for B; temperature and width for C; temperature for A). State explicitly when none exists.
2. Identify exactly which cells differ between E0/E1/E2 and which single value is decisive for Site B in each state.
3. Compute independently, showing arithmetic:
   a. Historical selection A=V1, B=V3, C=V3: committed cost, 8% contingency, total, headroom against £120,000.
   b. Under E2 with B=V4 and C=V3 (A=V1): committed cost, 8% contingency, total, headroom.
   c. Under E2 with B=V4 and C=V2 (A=V1): committed cost, 8% contingency, total, headroom.
   d. Maximum committed cost that leaves at least 8% contingency within £120,000; and with A=V1, C=V3 fixed, the Site B all-in ceiling; and with A=V1, C=V2 fixed, the Site B all-in ceiling.
4. Schedule arithmetic as of 2026-02-14: using the lead times, state the earliest delivery date if ordered on 2026-02-14 for each vendor, and whether that can fit the relevant installation window (Site A 5 Jan-27 Feb 2026; Site B 2 Mar-24 Apr 2026; Site C 4 May-26 Jun 2026). Also state the latest order date to be ready by the end of each window. Note any way the stated requirement "order before the window opens" affects this.
5. Check whether the prior independent check in /run/f1/world/deliverables/independent-check.md is still complete for the 2026-02-14 state; identify any gap.

Return a concise structured report with sections: Evidence states, Decisive values, Compliance matrices, Cost arithmetic, Schedule arithmetic, Gaps/discrepancies, Limitation. Do not edit files. Do not say any candidate is accepted.
Your parent agent id is "session-768ddf8f-bb99-4c3d-b2f6-f5ee0582bc5b". Before you finish, send your result to that agent with send_message({ agent_id: "session-768ddf8f-bb99-4c3d-b2f6-f5ee0582bc5b", message: "<self-contained result>" }). The parent shares your workspace but does not automatically receive your transcript, tool output, or reasoning. Send earlier messages as well when a finding changes what the parent should do next; sending a message does not end your turn.
